correctness.rationale: The transition matrices are row-stochastic and have rational entries in \( [0,1] \). For current accepting-state probability \(p\), the updates are \(f_a(p)=1/2+p/6\), \(f_b(p)=1/2-p/2\), and \(f_c(p)=1-2p/3\). Exact enumeration of all 27 length-three strings yields the unique maximum \(47/54\) at \(\mathtt{abc}\) and maximum competing value \(23/27\) at \(\mathtt{cbc}\), giving gap \(1/54\). A one-state PFA assigns equal acceptance probability to all inputs, so the minimum number of states is exactly two.

Gill's classification is for binary strings; its alphabet-extension corollary preserves complexity two for an already binary target, not a word containing three distinct symbols. value.rationale: The 2026 general theorem leaves a specific classification gap for alphabets of size at least three. This witness is minimal in both length and alphabet support for a word containing three distinct symbols, and it disproves the natural support-size extrapolation that only two-symbol words can have \(A_P=2\). The exact rational gap \(1/54\) makes it a reproducible boundary case for any future classification. The result does not overclaim a general theorem or optimal gap.
